notes: §1985:VI.6.10.3 SR1: "Mnemonic-name-1 is associated with a hardware device in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph in the Environment Division." BindDisplayUpon passes the UPON word to MnemonicDevice, which refuses it with COBOL0817 in three cases: no SPECIAL-NAMES entry in scope declares it as a mnemonic-name (MnemonicRegistry.TryUse over ConfigurationSlice.TryGetMnemonic, the unit's own entries and then its container's), the entry it names is a switch or a feature and not a device, or the device cannot receive data. The code has no edition arm and needs none: the devices are the implementor's four (CONSOLE, SYSOUT, SYSERR, SYSIN) at every edition, and the 2023 widening to a software device adds no name at 85. Probed at 85: UPON a mnemonic of CONSOLE or SYSERR accepted, in the declaring program and in a program contained in it, in either case of the word; UPON a data-name, an undeclared word, an alphabet-name, a class-name, a condition-name, the bare device-names CONSOLE and SYSOUT, a switch mnemonic, a C01 feature mnemonic and a SYSIN mnemonic all refused COBOL0817. The witness is UPON a data-name.

next.reason: 1985: 'Mnemonic-name-1 is associated with a hardware device in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph'. §2023:14.9.11.3 SR2 keeps the SPECIAL-NAMES association but widens the device to 'a hardware or software device capable of receiving data from the program'. No 1985 rule admits a software device. Receiving capability was already implied by the 1985 DISPLAY GR1 and GR4. Both are compile-time rules. §2023:12.3.7.3 SR7 limits where mnemonic-name-3 may be used and states no part of this rule.
